t.1.1: Janaka said: How does one attain knowledge? How will liberation come about? And how is dispassion attained? Tell me this, O Lord.
t.1.2: Aṣṭāvakra said: If you seek liberation, my child, shun the objects of the senses as poison, and cultivate forgiveness, sincerity, compassion, contentment and truth as nectar.
t.1.3: You are not earth, nor water, nor fire, nor air, nor sky. For liberation, know yourself as the Self, the witness of all these, whose very form is consciousness.
t.1.4: If you set the body apart and abide resting in pure consciousness, then this very moment you will become happy, peaceful, and freed from bondage.
t.1.5: You are not of the brahmin or any other caste, nor do you belong to any stage of life, nor are you an object of the senses. You are unattached and formless, the witness of the universe; be happy.
t.1.6: Dharma and adharma, pleasure and pain, belong to the mind, not to you, O all-pervading one. You will neither be the doer nor the enjoyer; you are ever free.
t.1.7: You alone will be the seer of all, and you are always all but free. This indeed is your bondage: that you see the seer as something other.
t.1.9: With the fire of the conviction "I am the One, pure awareness," burn down the dense forest of ignorance, and, free from sorrow, be happy.
t.1.8: You who have been bitten by the great black serpent of egoism, thinking "I am the doer," drink the nectar of the conviction "I am not the doer," and be happy.
t.1.10: That in which this universe appears, imagined like a snake in a rope, that bliss, supreme bliss, that awareness, you are; wander happily.
t.1.11: One who considers himself free is indeed free, and one who considers himself bound remains bound. True is the popular saying here in this world: as one thinks, so one becomes.
t.1.12: The Self is the witness, all-pervading, complete, one, free, pure consciousness, actionless, unattached, desireless and at peace. Only through delusion does it appear to be caught in saṃsāra.
t.1.13: Meditate on the Self as immovable awareness, free of duality, having let go of the delusion "I am a mere reflection" and of every state, outer as well as inner.
t.1.15: You are unattached, actionless, self-luminous and spotless. This indeed is your bondage: that you practise samādhi.
t.1.14: For a long time, my son, you have been bound by the noose of identification with the body. Cutting it with the sword of the knowledge 'I am awareness,' be happy.
t.1.16: This universe is pervaded by you and truly strung upon you. You are by nature pure consciousness; do not fall into smallness of mind.
t.1.18: Know that what has form is unreal, and that the formless is unmoving and permanent. Through this instruction in the truth, there is no further possibility of rebirth.
t.1.17: Be free of expectation, changeless, full and complete, cool of heart, of unfathomable understanding, and unperturbed, with your sole inclination resting in pure consciousness.
t.1.19: Just as the mirror exists both within and all around the form reflected in it, so the Supreme Lord exists both within and all around this body.
t.1.20: Just as the one all-pervading space is both outside and inside a pot, so the eternal, uninterrupted Brahman exists in the whole multitude of beings.
